thread.title: Document Security Systems: Unique Opportunity In Anti-Counterfeiting, Blockchain, And Cannabis - Document Security Systems, Inc (NYSEMKT:DSS)

author: Arthur Frentzel
title: Document Security Systems: Unique Opportunity In Anti-Counterfeiting, Blockchain, And Cannabis - Document Security Systems, Inc (NYSEMKT:DSS)
text:
Document Security Systems ( DSS ) presents a unique opportunity to participate in three high-growth business segments: anti-counterfeiting, blockchain, and cannabis, as well as IP licensing & monetization - all with one company. Although the company has been in business for decades, with an IPO in 2004, its technology has just begun to be recognized, which will be discussed in detail below. Since its IPO in 2004 the stock has experienced periods of extreme volatility and currently trades at a fraction of its IPO price. Continued erosion in the stock price necessitated a 1-for-4 reverse stock split in 2016, greatly reducing share count but providing a threshold for growth ahead.
In spite of past difficulties, however, DSS has exhibited impressive staying power and continues to focus on its core business of providing an anti-counterfeiting suite of products which have recently begun to gain traction. Due to the globalization of business and the huge growth in online sales, unfortunately the counterfeit business is booming. According to Global Brand Counterfeiting Report 2018-2020 , counterfeit product sales totaled $1.2 trillion in 2017, about 2.5% of trade which is expected to grow to $1.8 trillion by 2020. With massive growth in counterfeits, it is apparent that current systems in place to address counterfeiting are not working. Through its Digital Products Group, DSS supplies a cost-effective digital solution to validate authentic products and provide data on both authentic and counterfeit products with its AuthentiGuard suite of products.
With the advent of advanced printers and scanners to copy product logos and other proprietary media, companies have become increasingly vulnerable to brand counterfeiting. It has become apparent that advanced authentication techniques were needed to detect counterfeit products to protect the value of brands and safeguard brand-loyal consumers from being targets of counterfeiters. Most techniques require either adding labels or other marking media like holograms, to authenticate products. Adding labels to products requires additional processes in manufacturing and packaging, along with added equipment costs. In addition, holograms also can be copied or purchased for as little as one cent each online. AuthentiGuard utilizes a hidden mark that can be validated with a smart device while remaining hidden from the view would-be counterfeiters. The underlying technology is described in the abstract of a core patent which details key features of AuthentiGuard as “A system and method for hidden security feature detection, analysis, and authentication using a smart device…to be positioned within a range of distances and angles from a target document that includes hidden/covert security feature(s).” In addition to pointing out key features of AuthentiGuard, the foregoing evidences the strong IP surrounding the proprietary system developed by the company.
Beyond verification, efficient supply chain management necessitates data collection surrounding all aspects of the product, including the origin and location of product in stages of processing or in distribution channels. Data supplies critical information needed to address counterfeits, validate warranty product, or track progression through supply chains, which is transmitted to suppliers via cloud applications. In addition, a vast amount of valuable marketing data can be generated as goods are tracked through distribution. Most counterfeit tracking systems require specialized equipment to scan affected product in the verification process. AuthentiGuard utilizes embedded code, utilizing PRISM technology that is resistant to counterfeiting on copiers and scanners. The AuthentiGuard mark incorporates data concerning all aspects of product authenticity, origin, destination, expiration and more, which can be scanned with multiple devices including smartphones. As illustrated in the graphic below provided in a 2019 company presentation , AuthentiGuard provides a secure marking technology that is embedded into packing graphics, or the product itself, in pre-press standard printing/manufacturing processes.
(Source: Company presentation)
Utilizing the foregoing attributes, AuthentiGuard can be implemented at very small cost per unit of any product or component. In addition, due to the data component, AuthentiGuard can be employed across an entire supply chain. Many manufacturers have hundreds, or thousands, of suppliers that are part of bringing finished goods to market. Since their data systems are seldom linked, due largely to security issues, they are not interoperable.
Blockchain Marc Andreessen, a co-developer of the original Netscape browser and Facebook ( FB ) director, has called blockchain "the most important technology since the internet" and many analysts are predicting revenue generated with blockchain in the trillions of dollars. AuthentiGuard is particularly well suited for the deployment of blockchain networks, which can enable much wider use of product data across supply chains internationally. In March, DSS announced a research partnership to develop and implement advanced tracking utilizing blockchain technology. The DSS blockchain offering is designated AuthentiChain. Beyond counterfeit monitoring, blockchain offers a means to more efficiently manage supply chains from a central network that does not compromise security of and data in the networks of individual companies. The effectiveness of AuthentiGuard, both in anti-counterfeiting and in blockchain deployment, along with the low cost of implementation, should ultimately lead to much greater adoption as companies recognize the merits of the technology and its differentiation from lesser alternatives.
While there are several competing systems in place to track and authenticate products, none appear to offer the robust features available in AuthentiGuard with minimal expenditures in applying the tracking media and in real time tracking. For example, RFID (radio frequency identification) is currently being utilized by many retailers to track merchandise within their facilities and, in some cases, facilitate transactions. One example is with Amazon Go (NASDAQ: AMZN ) convenience stores that enable customers to select and purchase items without going through checkout lanes. Selected items are tracked and billed utilizing a smart device app. Other retailers like Walmart (NYSE: WMT ) utilize RFID to track product within their facilities and supply chain, as well as to assist in keeping merchandise at the point-of-sale in stores. While RFID tracking is feature-rich, it requires major expenditures in labeling and hardware deployment, which may not be suitable for millions of products brought to market by the majority of suppliers. In addition, AuthentiGuard can be integrated with RFID tracking systems to extend anti-counterfeiting capabilities and enhance customer experience.
Beyond advantages for business, AuthentiGuard offers anti-counterfeiting functionality to consumers. With a smartphone, end consumers can check the authenticity of products for sale in making purchase decisions, especially for high-end items like watches, jewelry, electronics, handbags, pharmaceutical products, and personal care items. In pharmaceuticals alone, there is a vast market in which consumers purchase medications both online and from offshore pharmacies with no assurances of product authenticity and, most importantly, safety.
To fully appreciate the value of the DSS product offering in blockchain, an understanding of how blockchain works is essential. IBM ( IBM ) provides a free download of "Blockchain for Dummies" (2nd IBM Limited Edition) published by John Wiley & Sons, Inc., which could dramatically increase reader knowledge of how blockchain networks work and the essential requirement of authentication.
Business deployment Document Security Systems announced in 2017 that the company had been selected for international deployment of AuthentiGuard for a U.S.-based Fortune 50 company, which is currently under development. The announcement was the first of its kind in a major deployment. The system will include both anti-counterfeit monitoring and verification of product integrity in warranty returns. According to a report , about 1.4% of revenue is paid out for warranty claims. While manufacturing processes are subjected to continual improvement, warranty exposure for manufacturers continues to be affected by the explosion of complexity of new products and features available. And with commodity-type components, it is often difficult to quickly verify that products returned for warranty credit were in fact originally supplied by a company.
In addition, DSS continues to work with prospective clients and expects to announce new business agreements in the coming months, which should be a major boost to recognition of the AuthentiGuard suite of products. To further extend its reach, the company announced in 2017 an agreement with Sun Chemical to cross-market brand protection technologies. Sun Chemical is a leading supplier of printing inks, coatings, and materials, which is a division of DIC Corporation, a $7.5 billion conglomerate with 20,000 employees.
DSS Plastics Group According to Form 10K , the DSS plastics group “manufactures laminated and surface printed cards which can include magnetic stripes, bar codes, holograms, signature panels, invisible ink, micro fine printing, guilloche patterns, biometric, radio frequency identification (RFID) and watermarks for printed plastic documents such as ID cards, event badges, and driver’s licenses.” The plastics ID business alone is multi-billion dollar industry, which could provide significant growth for the company as AuthentiGuard gains traction.
DSS Packaging and Printing Group The Packaging and Printing Group produces custom paperboard packaging serving clients in the pharmaceutical, beverage, photo packaging, toy, specialty foods and direct marketing industries, among others. The group also provides secure and commercial printing services for end-user customers and a wide array of printed materials such as security paper, vital records, prescription paper, birth certificates, receipts, manuals, identification materials, entertainment tickets, secure coupons, parts tracking forms, brochures, direct mailing pieces, catalogs, business cards, etc. Printed products currently represent about 90% of revenue (Source: Form 10K ). During full-year 2017 two customers, Walgreens and Shutterfly, represented 46% of DSS revenue in the purchase of packaging in their photo processing businesses.
Cannabis In November, DSS announced the introduction of comprehensive brand protection and packaging design solutions exclusively for the cannabis industry to be supplied by the DSS Premier Packaging division. Brand protected packaging is particularly well suited to the cannabis industry for developing supply chains. Counterfeit product could be relatively easy to produce, sell, and distribute, copying brands that are just beginning to gain traction. In addition, the cannabis industry is highly regulated and, in some cases, producers are required to track all stages of the product from “seed to finished product.” In addition, documentation is required to verify that taxes and/or duties have been paid. Beyond brand protection with AuthentiGuard, DSS will offer custom folding cartons tailored to cannabis as well as materials management, logistics, and inventory management. As quoted by Mike Tobin, DSS VP, Sales and Marketing “We can provide companies with a comprehensive, very secure solution starting with a digital signature on the packaging all the way through to consumer engagement, including a blockchain-based option.” Utilizing AuthentiGuard, end consumers can authenticate products with a smartphone. Further, AuthentiGuard can be integrated with GPS systems to track illegal product movement.
Due to the ability to integrate secure authentication and data tracking capabilities into packaging, DSS possesses unique advantages in gaining traction in the cannabis industry, which offers an opportunity for investors to participate in the segment without having to pick cannabis players with extremely high valuations. In addition to advantages for suppliers, authentication is critical in consumables when safety becomes a major concern for consumers. The strength of the DSS product offering is likely to gain significant traction in the developing cannabis industry. While intense competition for packaging will undoubtedly emerge in cannabis, DSS appears to have clear advantages when compared to competition that may offer packaging only.

To focus more on the core business of anti-counterfeiting, DSS has restructured the IP enforcement business in agreements with third parties to fund most of the expenses associated with litigation while maintaining some of the upside in successful outcomes. In spite of this, potential gains to the company remain significant. In the case of the Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) litigation, Markman hearings are in progress and the company is awaiting results which are expected at any time. A positive outcome from the hearings could be a significant catalyst to the stock.
In view of the foregoing business segments described, DSS maintains a robust and diversified pipeline for growth, which is illustrated in the graphic below.

Expanding Asian Market In September of 2017, DSS announced entry into international markets with the creation of DSS International, focusing initially on China and the Asian markets through its wholly-owned subsidiary DSS Asia Ltd. Then on January 23, the company announced an expansion in China with an acquisition of Guangzhou HotApp Technology Ltd, which will provide technology development, product sales, and customer support in Guangzhou, China. Further, the acquisition provides necessary licenses to operate successfully in the China market.
Financials In spite of a history of losses, DSS has maintained moderate financial strength for a microcap. As of the end of Q3, the key financial metrics were as follows (in millions USD, source Form 10Q) .

With a current market cap near a tiny $16 million and about 17 million shares outstanding, the stock provides an opportunity that is just beginning to gain traction. Revenue over the past 5 years has grown at only 1.7% annually, totaling $18.4 million for the last four quarters. As revenue begins to ramp in any of its four business segments, the market will recognize the opportunity quickly. Business wins should also provide significant catalysts for the shares which currently trade near $1.06.
Management The DSS management team includes a roster of veterans who are capable of executing the business plan to success. Jeff Ronaldi has been CEO and a director at DSS since 2013 and formerly served as CEO of Lexington Technology Group, which was acquired by DSS in 2012. Mr. Ronaldi has over 25 years of experience of successfully managing tech-related business. Other key members of top management have been with the company multiple years and CFO Philip Jones has been with the company since 2005. David Wicker, VP of R&D, has been with DSS since 2002 when a company he founded was purchased by the company. Mike Tobin, VP of Marketing and Product Management, joined the company in 2016 with 25 years of experience marketing technology and telecom products to enterprise, B2B, government, and consumer target markets.
Beyond executive management, since 2015 the DSS board has been enhanced with five new directors, who are highly capable and focused on technology investing. Mr. Heng Fai Ambrose Chan, who was appointed in 2017, has vast experience in Asian markets and serves as CEO of wholly owned subsidiary DSS International. Mr. Chan has aggressively purchased DSS shares and, as of the last Form 4 , owns a major portion of outstanding shares.
All executive management and board members as a group currently own about 28% of outstanding shares and have been continuous buyers on the open market with three board members holding more than a million shares each.
Upcoming catalysts Beyond revenue gains for business currently in place, several catalysts could drive DSS shares higher in the near term and throughout 2019. Due to ongoing development work with new prospective clients in the AuthentiGuard business, new business announcements are likely. Likewise, business wins could be announced in the cannabis space which could gain wide recognition in the market. In addition, success in the IP monetization space could offer the prospect of significant revenue upside with limited expenses incurred.
Risks Document Security Systems currently operates as a tiny microcap company with limited financial resources. The company has a history of losses and, in the absence proven revenue growth in its businesses, represents a speculative investment that may not be suitable for some investors. While the author believes the company will be a profitable investment for many investors, the stock has a history of extreme volatility that should be considered. Readers should not invest in the company based solely on the content of this article, and do so only after full consideration of risks outlined in Form 10K beginning on page 8.
Conclusion After a long period of developing its IP and product offerings, it appears DSS is positioned for significant growth ahead in anti-counterfeiting/brand protection, cannabis authentication and packaging, and IP monetization. At the current stock price, DSS represents an out-sized opportunity for aggressive investors to purchase shares below the cost paid by insiders in recent transactions for an opportunity to participate in the high-growth markets described above. Significant catalysts, including new customer announcements and increasing revenue, are likely to power the shares higher as the value of DSS product offerings becomes evident.
Disclosure: I am/we are long DSS.
